seo-description: Step-by-step guide to run a node on the Sintrop impact blockchain with Docker or the prebuilt client, on mainnet or the Sequoia testnet.
footerTagline: A public proof-of-work blockchain for social and environmental impact applications.
heroLead: Every node makes Sintrop harder to censor and easier to trust. Sync a full copy of the chain, relay transactions, and — if you mine — earn SIN for every block you find.
why1Desc: More independent nodes means more censorship resistance and no single party that can rewrite history.
why2Desc: Miners receive newly minted SIN for each block they find. There is no pre-mine — mining is the only source of new coins.
why3Desc: A container on a spare machine, a dedicated server, CPU or GPU mining. Mainnet or the Sequoia testnet for practice.
why4Desc: We encourage every operator to use solar, wind, hydro or other low-impact energy. The goal is a mostly renewable network.
need1: A machine that can stay online — Linux is easiest for mining
need2: Docker, or the ability to run the prebuilt client for your OS
need3: Disk space for the full chain, plus a stable internet connection
need4: A wallet address to receive mining rewards (any EVM address)
need5: For a public server: a fixed IP and port 25225 forwarded to the machine
builderLead: Pick your options and copy the exact commands.
builderWalletHint: Pasted into the commands below as miner.etherbase. You can change it later from the node console.
builderWalletInvalid: That doesn't look like a 0x address — the commands will still use it verbatim.
stepPrereqDocker: Install Docker for your operating system and make sure the daemon is running.
stepPrereqBinary: You only need a terminal and permission to run the downloaded binary.
stepGetBinary: Download the latest go-sintrop release for your OS from GitHub, then extract it and open a terminal in that folder.
stepGetDockerClone: Clone the client repository and build the image:
stepStartBinaryDesc: Run the client from the release folder. The node syncs a full copy of the chain and opens a console.
stepStartDockerDesc: Run the image, mapping the P2P and RPC ports and mounting a folder for the chain data. Replace the host path with a directory on your machine.
stepStartDockerGeth: Inside the container, start the node:
stepMineDesc: In the node console, begin CPU mining. Rewards go to the address you set above.
stepMineGpu: For GPU mining, keep the node running and point a compatible miner at the local RPC port instead.
stepVerifyDesc: In the console, confirm the node sees peers and is following the chain head.
stepStopNote: To stop the node safely, press Ctrl + D in the console.
operateLead: Common commands to run inside the geth console.
bootnodeDesc: A bootnode with a fixed public IP helps new nodes discover the network. It uses the same client with a slightly different setup.
